intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by mutation in the dynactin gene (DCTN1; 601143) on chromosome 2p13.1.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by mutation in the dynactin gene (DCTN1).
checks.evidence_quote: Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that a dynactin mutation causes a lower motor neuron disease. It does not use the name HMND14 or say the inheritance is autosomal dominant (only the abstract was supplied).

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene is located on chromosome 2p13.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract places the gene at 2p13. The 2p13.1 band is standard nomenclature that restates this location.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is a lower motor neuron disease. Puls et al. (2003) showed that it is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is a lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a lower motor neuron disease but does not call it autosomal dominant distal HMN-14.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) showed that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change
checks.explanation: The mutation in the gene for the largest dynactin subunit is supported. The disease name HMND14 and autosomal dominant inheritance are not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Dynactin is an axonal transport protein.
checks.evidence_quote: encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The abstract calls dynactin an axonal transport protein.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) studied a lower motor neuron disease and mapped the disease locus to chromosome 2p13 by linkage analysis. The linked interval contained the DCTN1 gene.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) used linkage analysis to map the locus for a lower motor neuron disease to chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports linkage of the disease to 2p13.

checks.claim: The chromosome 2p13 linkage interval for the lower motor neuron disease studied by Puls et al. (2003) contained the DCTN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The gene for the largest dynactin subunit (DCTN1) lies in the linked interval.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) analysed the DCTN1 gene, which lies in the 2p13 linkage interval and encodes the largest subunit of dynactin. In patients with lower motor neuron disease, they found a single base-pair change resulting in an amino acid substitution. The substitution was predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain. In binding assays, the mutant protein bound microtubules less well than normal protein. Puls et al. (2003) concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene lies in the 2p13 linkage interval for the lower motor neuron disease studied by Puls et al. (2003).
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The abstract places the gene in the linked interval.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene encodes the largest subunit of dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the gene encodes the largest subunit of dynactin.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) found a single base-pair change in the DCTN1 gene, resulting in an amino acid substitution, in patients with lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a single base-pair change causing an amino acid substitution.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 amino acid substitution found by Puls et al. (2003) was predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain.
checks.evidence_quote: an amino-acid substitution that is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain

checks.claim: In binding assays, the mutant DCTN1 protein found by Puls et al. (2003) bound microtubules less well than normal protein.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports decreased microtubule binding by the mutant protein.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: This is the authors' stated conclusion.
